learning_outcomes.text: Generic knowledge of Machine Maintenance and Diagnostics, as well as its location in the industrial and productive context.
Knowledge of fundamental concepts, techniques, and methods in the field of machine maintenance and diagnostics.
Ability to analyze, evaluate, and organize activities specific to machine maintenance and diagnostics.
Ability to identify the causes of machine, equipment, and installation failures, as well as to propose improvements to prevent failures.
Ability to operate a maintenance program.
Design the basic architecture of a maintenance program.

syllabus_topics: Types of Maintenance. Legal Maintenance. Indicators
Planning and Management of Equipment and Service Maintenance
Maintenance Organization. Spare Parts. Budget and Budgetary Control. RCM and TPM
Fundamentals of Machine Operation. Equipment and Service Maintenance

Machine Diagnostics I: Instrumentation and Measurement Techniques. Practical cases applied to general industry and specific cases applied to desalination, automotive, and electric motors. Non-Destructive Testing
Machine Diagnostics II: Diagnostic Methods. Practical cases. Measurement, Assembly, and Quality Control Techniques
Occupational Risk Prevention. Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
teaching_methods: Theoretical and problem-solving classes for the full group
Practical classes in the classroom for medium or full groups
Seminars or other complementary activities for full or reduced groups
Attendance to tutorials, in-person and/or virtual, for reduced groups
Completion of field practices for full or reduced groups
assessment_rules: For continuous evaluation, a minimum grade of 5.0 is required in each theoretical-practical development exam and in the reports and assignments. The final grade is the weighted average of the two partial exams (40% each) and reports/assignments (20%), provided a minimum grade of 5.0 is obtained in each component. If the minimum grade is not met in a component, the final grade will be a failing grade with the numerical weighted average if below 5, otherwise 4. Unpassed partial exams can be recovered in the first official call; if both partials are failed, the student must retake the entire subject in the second call. For single evaluation, a specific theoretical-practical exam (80%) and a practical content evaluation (20%) will be conducted. Attendance to at least 80% of practical classes and completion of all practical reports are mandatory to pass the practical content; students who do not complete practicals may request a practical exam and must obtain a minimum of 5.0.
